title: Human Resource Generalist
company: East Texas Lighthouse for the Blind
description:
The purpose of the East Texas Lighthouse for the Blind shall be the rehabilitation, education, training and employment of people who are blind and visually impaired, and the furtherance of their interests and welfare through programs designed to provide rehabilitation, training and employment opportunities, being wholly charitable and benevolent.

GENERAL SUMMARY OF POSITION

The Human Resource Generalist is an indirect non-exempt, labor support position. The HR Generalist is responsible for assisting the Director of Human Resources with the daily functions of the employment life cycle, including but not limited to benefits, recruiting, onboarding, off boarding, etc.

EXPECTATIONS FOR ALL EMPLOYEES

Support the organization's mission, vision, and values by exhibiting the following behaviors: excellence and competence, collaboration, innovation, honesty, respect for others, commitment to our community, and accountability and ownership.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES

Human Resources Administration & Records

  • Maintains accurate, up-to-date, and confidential HR files, records, and documentation.
  • Performs periodic audits of HR files and records to ensure required documents are complete, accurate, and properly filed, including I-9s, self-reporting, and other required documentation.
  • Performs routine administrative tasks required to administer and execute HR programs.
  • Provides administrative support in Paycom, including payroll, timekeeping, reporting, data entry, and related functions.
  • Cross-trains in all functions of Human Resources.

Employee Relations & HR Support

  • Acts as a resource for employees regarding HR policies, procedures, and practices.
  • Answers frequently asked questions from applicants and employees regarding standard HR practices and refers more complex matters to appropriate senior-level staff.
  • Monitors and responds to HR Helpdesk and Text’em inquiries.
  • Serves as a witness to disciplinary meetings, terminations, and investigations as requested.
  • Participates in at least one employee-related committee.
  • Assists the Safety Committees as needed

Recruitment & Onboarding

  • Recruits, interviews, and facilitates the hiring of qualified applicants for open positions.
  • Collaborates with department managers to understand the skills, competencies, and qualifications required for open positions.
  • Assists with all aspects of new hire orientation and onboarding.
  • Schedules post-employment training, including benefits orientation, mission-focused training, immersion training, safety training, and other required training.
  • Communicates and works with temporary staffing agencies to fulfill staffing needs.
  • Conducts background checks for volunteers across all ETLB divisions.

Benefits & Leave Administration

  • Assists with the annual benefits open enrollment process.
  • Manages all leave of absence policies and requests.
  • Assists employees and management with benefit-related questions and issues.

Payroll, Timekeeping & Garnishments

  • Provides administrative support to Payroll, including answering questions, distributing checks, and communicating payroll-related information.
  • Assists with Paycom payroll and timekeeping functions.

Compliance & Reporting

  • Responsible for maintaining compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations.
  • Conducts mandatory reporting and compliance filings, including VETS-100, EEO-1, AAP, and other required reports.
  • Prepares reporting and audit packets for federal and state contracts, including NIB, WorkQuest, and other applicable contracts.
  • Establishes and leads compliance training, including annual HR compliance training.
  • Reviews, tracks, and documents compliance with mandatory and non-mandatory training, continuing education, and general organizational policies.

Unemployment, Drug Screening & Other HR Processes

  • Assist with unemployment claims and related documentation.
  • Assist with the random drug screening process.

Employee Engagement & Activities

  • Leads the Employee Activities Committee, including event planning, budgeting, facilitation, and execution of employee events and holiday activities.
  • Coordinates and assists with large-scale employee meetings and events.
  • Obtains and processes expenses for company gifts, prizes, and employee incentives.
  • Initiates and coordinates national and state-level award nomination and application processes.
  • Creates and distributes weekly Toolbox Talks.

Transportation & Site Coordination

  • Serves as a liaison between organizational sites regarding tours and visits for Client Services and outside parties.

General Administrative Support

  • Assists with special projects and organizational initiatives as needed.
  • Participates in meetings, seminars, committees, and other organizational activities as requested.
  • Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

title: REMOVABLES TECHNICIAN
description:

Headquartered in Savannah, GA, Pan-Am has two additional locations in Houston, TX and Sandy, UT – allowing us to serve a base of clients covering the entire country.

Position Summary

The Pan-Am Removable Denture Technician will specialize in acrylic processing and post processing functions within the removable department. This role is crucial in ensuring that all dentures meet the highest standards of fit, function and aesthetics.

title: Digital Services Lead
description:
Salary: Wellbeing benefits + Growth + Flexible working

About the role

We’re working with a Taupō-based organisation looking for an experienced Digital Services Lead to lead and develop its digital service environment.

This is a broad people and service leadership role spanning workplace technology, digital and application support, information management and digital coordination. You’ll lead a multidisciplinary team, take end-to-end ownership across digital services and help ensure they remain reliable while continuing to improve how people across the organisation experience and use technology.

There is a strong improvement focus. You’ll use service data, user feedback and business needs to identify where services can work better, whether through automation, self-service, improved processes or changes to the way support is delivered.

Information management is also an important part of the role. You’ll help strengthen how organisational information and records are governed, managed and used so they remain trusted, accessible and secure.

You’ll work across the organisation, building relationships with stakeholders and suppliers, understanding what people need from digital services and helping connect those needs with organisational priorities, technology roadmaps and future ways of working.

A key part of the opportunity is helping shift digital services from reactive delivery toward more proactive business enablement, better user experiences and measurable value.

What you’ll be doing

  • Leading, coaching and developing a multidisciplinary digital services team

  • Taking end-to-end ownership across workplace technology, digital and application support, and information management

  • Leading the planning, prioritisation and delivery of projects and initiatives across the team’s portfolio

  • Using service data, user feedback and performance measures to identify opportunities for improvement

  • Supporting automation, self-service, prevention and process improvement

  • Leading and strengthening information and records management capability, governance and lifecycle practices

  • Helping ensure information remains trusted, accessible, secure and available to support operational and organisational needs

  • Managing technology suppliers, monitoring performance and progressing service improvements where needed

  • Working across the organisation to understand user needs and improve digital experiences

  • Helping align digital services with organisational priorities, technology roadmaps and future ways of working

  • Working collaboratively with other digital and data capability to support better use of information, analytics and emerging technology

What we’re looking for:

We’re interested in experienced digital services or IT leaders who combine strong service judgement with good people leadership and an improvement mindset.

You’ll ideally bring:

  • Substantial background across IT support and/or information management, including demonstrated team leadership or supervisory responsibility

  • Proven service ownership from a user and service-delivery perspective

  • A solid understanding of modern workplace technologies, digital support environments and information lifecycle considerations

  • Good working knowledge of IT service management practices

  • Confident people leadership, with the ability to coach, develop and set clear expectations for a multidisciplinary team

  • Clear communication and relationship-building skills across technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Confidence managing suppliers and external service providers

  • The ability to use service information, feedback and performance measures to improve delivery

  • Comfortable balancing multiple service areas and competing priorities

  • Sound judgement when weighing user experience, service performance, risk and organisational needs

  • A continuous-improvement mindset and an interest in finding better ways to deliver digital services

Relevant industry qualifications or DevOps Foundation/practical DevOps leadership experience would be advantageous.

What’s on offer?

This is an opportunity to lead across a broad digital services portfolio and influence how people experience and use technology across the organisation.

You’ll also be joining an organisation that offers:

  • Flexible, family-friendly working

  • Wellbeing support and employee benefits

  • Career development and growth opportunities

  • A strong focus on supporting people to develop their strengths

Keen to learn more?

If you’re an experienced digital services or IT leader who enjoys developing people, improving how services work and making technology easier and more useful for the people who rely on it, this is worth a conversation.

title: Pharmacy Tech Navigator (5729)
description:
Regional One Health is currently seeking a Certified Pharmacy Technican Navigator.

Must have National Certification such as PTCB or NHA AND TN Pharmacy Tech License to qualify

A Brief Overview
The Certified Pharmacy Technician Clinic Navigator, will collaborate with comprehensive interdisciplinary roles as part of the Clinic care team to eliminate barriers to medication adherence. Provide members with medication access, adherence and affordability services, identifying and communicating discrepancies to build long-term solutions and connect patients and care team to pharmacy resources and support enrollment in qualifying copay assistance programs. This position acts as a medication therapy liaison and navigator for the patient, the clinic care team and providers and also serves as pharmacist extender, performing administrative and clinical support tasks to enhance the delivery of comprehensive medication management services.

What you will do

  • Adopt the Challenger sales model; a sales methodology that focuses on teaching customers about the value of a product or service while also challenging their assumptions and beliefs. Ability to sale the solution to a problem.
  • Serve as the pharmacy team’s first line of triage and subject matter expert for medication access and affordability needs including prior authorizations (PA), PA appeals, copay assistance, rx billing issues with the pharmacy, med synchronization, and home delivery.
  • Provide ongoing education on medication access and affordability tools and resources.
  • Connect uninsured or underinsured to an eligibility expert to explore assistance that best fits the patient’s needs.
  • Provide ongoing care team education on medication access and affordability tools and resources.
  • Connect patient’s referred or identified as eligible requiring a pharmacist consult ; perform reminder phone calls and appointment rescheduling as necessary.
  • Provide patients with a direct line of communication with provider and pharmacy staff.
  • Provide emotional and social support to help patient’s access financial and social resources within the organization.
  • Responsible for accepting new prescriptions and making sure all necessary information including insurance verification is available to process orders.
  • Explains all company programs and services to patients and physician’s office staff.
  • Communicates with patients as needed based on prescription refills and refers any medication or illness related questions or concerns to a board licensed healthcare profession including but not limited to: nurses, pharmacists, or supervised pharmacy interns.
  • Responsible for scheduling prescription refills within the pharmacy software.
  • Contacts patients to schedule deliveries, confirm address, inform of any co-payment involved and notify of payment responsibilities.
  • Assists with prior authorizations.
  • Refers under or uninsured patients to appropriate patient assistance programs and helps with applications.
  • Communicates patient status to physician’s offices/clinics.
  • Maintains patient confidentiality.
  • Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned.
  • Utilize operating systems and tools to help manage patient therapy and refill compliance.
  • Regular attendance in conformance with the standards, which may be established from time to time, is essential to the successful performance of this position. Upon employment, all employees are required to fully comply with Regional One Health policies and regulations.

title: Partner Forward Deployed Engineer, Generative AI, Google Cloud (Japanese, English)

title: Software Engineer, Google Cloud Platform, Fault Management
description:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a Staff Software Engineer on the Server RAS team, you will bridge hardware and software across Google's compute fleet. You will apply a first-principles, data-driven approach to eliminate fleet failure modes, maximize availability, and lower total cost of ownership (TCO).

You will drive hardware/software co-design by collaborating with silicon vendors and shaping industry standards. Leveraging your deep expertise at the hardware/software boundary, you will architect advanced CPU, Memory (DDR5+) and high-speed I/O bus (PCIe, CXL) error-handling mechanisms.

Additionally, you will design fault-tolerant software frameworks to minimize customer impact, partner with platform teams to validate advanced Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) capabilities, and automate telemetry pipelines for real-time fault isolation.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

US: $207000 - $300000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Design and develop highly scalable software and firmware systems that detect, diagnose, and mitigate reliability issues across Google's server fleet

title: Controls Integration Engineer, One MHS | Systems Integration and Flow
description:
The Controls Integration Engineer is responsible for the on-site deployment, integration, and commissioning of automated material handling equipment such as sorters, conveyor systems, and Automated work cells. This role is highly execution-focused and hands-on, owning the technical bring-up of Industrial PCs (IPCs), PLCs, industrial networks, and field devices during installation and commissioning phases.
The engineer serves as a technical authority on-site, partnering closely with contractors, system integrators, vendors, and internal engineering teams to ensure systems are installed, tested, and commissioned safely, reliably, and in accordance with project standards and operational requirements.



Key job responsibilities
Deployment & Commissioning
• Execute on-site commissioning activities for sorters, conveyors, and automated work cells.
• Provision, configure, and validate Linux-based IPCs, PLCs, HMIs, industrial networks, and field devices per project standards.
• Perform I/O checkouts, network validation, and phased system bring-up activities.
• Execute commissioning and test plans, including sequencing, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
• Support dry runs, functional testing, and integrated system testing through startup and handover.
Troubleshooting & Technical Support
• Serve as the primary on-site technical resource for controls, networking, and system integration issues.
• Diagnose and resolve industrial networking problems (e.g., IP conflicts, VLAN issues, switch configuration, fieldbus communication faults).
• Troubleshoot PLC logic, device configuration, safety interlocks, and system-level faults across electrical, controls, and mechanical boundaries.
• Perform structured root-cause analysis and support implementation of permanent corrective actions.
• Document issues, resolutions, and lessons learned to support continuous improvement and future deployments.
On-Site Technical Leadership
• Provide day-to-day technical direction to technicians, electricians, and commissioning support personnel during system deployment.
• Coordinate closely with system integrators, OEMs, and internal stakeholders to resolve technical issues and unblock progress.
• Ensure compliance with safety requirements, quality standards, and commissioning best practices during installation and testing.
Integration & Handover
• Validate equipment functionality against design specifications, controls standards, and operational requirements.
• Support integration of equipment into Warehouse Control Systems (WCS) and higher-level orchestration layers.
• Participate in turnover activities, ensuring systems are stable, documented, and ready for operational ownership.
Continuous Improvement
• Identify opportunities to improve commissioning efficiency, reliability, and repeatability.
• Contribute to the development and refinement of commissioning tools, test procedures, and deployment standards.
• Provide feedback to design and integration teams to improve future system designs and deployment outcomes.

title: Food Services Volunteer Liaison
description:
JOB Summary:

The Food Services Volunteer Liaison is responsible for ensuring an excellent volunteer experience within the Food Services Department and for serving as the primary bridge between the kitchen and the Volunteer Department. This position coordinates all aspects of Food Services volunteer involvement for approximately 3,000 meals per day, including scheduling support, orientation, on site guidance, and communication of needs and feedback between departments.

The Food Services Volunteer Liaison ensures that volunteers understand their roles in the kitchen and on the serving line, are trained to work safely, and perform tasks to the satisfaction of the kitchen team, while feeling welcomed, valued, and connected to The Midnight Mission’s purpose.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1. Volunteer Experience and Hospitality

  • Welcome all Food Services volunteers upon arrival, individually or in groups, ensuring they feel seen, appreciated, and oriented.

  • Provide a brief, mission centered introduction to TMM and explain how their volunteer work supports the daily meal operation.

  • Serve as the primary on shift point of contact for volunteer questions and basic problem solving within Food Services.

  • Promote a culture of dignity, respect, and gratitude toward volunteers among all Food Services staff and work therapy participants.

2. Liaison to the Volunteer Department

  • Partner closely with the Volunteer Department to coordinate Food Services volunteer needs, priorities, and coverage.

  • Communicate daily and weekly volunteer needs for the kitchen, prep, dishwashing, sack lunches, and line service so the Volunteer Department can recruit and schedule appropriately.

  • Confirm group details, including size, age range, accessibility needs, and any special considerations, in advance of their visit.

  • Provide timely feedback to the Volunteer Department about volunteer performance, group dynamics, concerns, and exceptional contributions.

  • Collaborate on volunteer recognition efforts, such as thank you communications, photos when appropriate, and invitations to return.

  • Participate in regular check ins or meetings with the Volunteer Department to review trends, upcoming events, and improvement opportunities.

3. Scheduling and Shift Coordination

  • Review daily and weekly volunteer schedules provided by the Volunteer Department to ensure alignment with kitchen needs.

  • Confirm volunteer assignments for each shift, matching group size and abilities with appropriate tasks.

  • Communicate any changes in kitchen operations, meal service, or staffing that may affect volunteer use and coordinate adjustments as needed.

  • Support day of adjustments such as late arrivals, no shows, or unexpected groups by reassigning tasks or contacting the Volunteer Department when necessary.

4. Orientation, Training, and Role Clarity

  • Provide concise, role specific orientation at the start of each shift that covers:

  • Safety and sanitation practices

  • Confidentiality and respectful engagement with guests

  • Kitchen rules and expectations

  • Specific tasks and reporting structure for the shift

  • Demonstrate assigned tasks such as food prep, serving on the line, dishwashing, assembling lunches, and basic cleaning.

  • Check for understanding by having volunteers repeat instructions or briefly demonstrate the task.

  • Reinforce expectations and answer questions throughout the shift so volunteers remain confident and effective.

  • Maintain and update written quick guides, signage, and training materials for volunteer tasks in collaboration with the Kitchen Manager and Food Services Manager.

5. On Site Oversight and Quality Assurance

  • Circulate regularly through volunteer work areas, including prep stations, serving line, dish area, and packing tables.

  • Monitor volunteer performance and provide real time coaching to ensure tasks are completed to kitchen standards for quality, safety, and efficiency.

  • Identify mismatches between a volunteer’s ability or comfort level and their assignment, and make appropriate reassignments in consultation with the Kitchen Manager or line lead.

  • Ensure volunteers are actively engaged and not left without clear work during the shift, identifying additional appropriate tasks when primary work is complete.

6. Safety, Sanitation, and Compliance

  • Ensure volunteers comply with all required safety and sanitation procedures, including proper handwashing, glove use, hair restraints, and prohibited items in food areas.

  • Reinforce Department of Health and internal policy requirements in a supportive and clear manner.

  • Respond promptly to spills, hazards, and incidents, and notify the Kitchen Manager or Food Services Manager according to protocol.

  • Support staff in maintaining a clean, organized environment in volunteer accessible areas.

7. Communication and Collaboration

  • Maintain ongoing communication with the Food Services Manager and Kitchen Manager regarding volunteer needs, performance, and operational priorities.

  • Attend Food Services and volunteer related meetings as requested, providing updates on volunteer engagement and key issues.

  • Work collaboratively with staff across departments to support special events, holiday meals, and catering where volunteers are involved.

  • Model professional, trauma informed communication with guests, staff, and volunteers at all times.

8. Documentation, Data, and Reporting

  • Verify volunteer attendance for Food Services shifts and ensure sign in sheets or electronic records are complete and accurate.

  • Provide the Volunteer Department with timely, accurate volunteer hour data, including individual and group totals, as directed.

  • Track key volunteer engagement information for Food Services such as frequently returning groups, peak times, and gaps in coverage.

  • Prepare simple periodic summaries or reports on volunteer utilization, challenges, and recommendations for improving volunteer integration into kitchen operations.

description:

The Under the Roof Labor Planning Technology (UTRPT) team is looking for a Software Development Engineer to join us in creating solutions that power Amazon's labor planning capabilities.

title: Senior Partner Solutions Architect, Manufacturing
description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Partner Solutions Architect (PSA) to join the AWS Partner Growth & Strategy (PG&S) team supporting Independent Software Vendor (ISV) partners in manufacturing. In this role, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor to strategic ISV partners, helping them architect, build, and optimize their solutions on AWS. You will drive deep technical engagement with ISV partners to imagine new product offerings, accelerate their cloud adoption, validate joint solutions, and enable go-to-market success through co-engineering efforts, technical enablement, and solution design.

As a PSA in the Partner Growth & Strategy (PG&S) Organization, you will combine broad technical expertise with strong relationship-building skills to influence partner technology decisions, identify strategic wins, and deliver customer value through partner-led solutions. You will work at the intersection of partner strategy and hands-on technical delivery, bridging business outcomes with cloud architecture best practices. You will provide our partners and customers with the expertise and scale needed to build innovative solutions for their most critical challenges.

Our goal is to help these partners build, go-to-market and, sell solutions leveraging AWS programs and capabilities across a range of cloud and AI services. We need a self-driven individual who thrives on continuous learning and working with the latest technologies to produce results that impact customers.

The ideal candidate brings:
- An inclination to get hands-on with diverse technologies to deepen understanding and create working concepts
- Customer-facing skills that would allow you to represent AWS well with partners and customers
- The ability to drive productive discussions with senior business and technical personnel
- A broad and deep technical background that bolsters credibility when offering guidance to engineers and architects
- Experience as a thought leader who can capture the attention of decision-makers through channels such as written publications, video, social media, and speaking engagements at industry conferences
- A knack for thinking strategically across business, product, and technical domains
- 30% travel is required

Key job responsibilities
- Develop technology strategy and senior level relationships with strategic manufacturing partners
- Serve as the primary technical advisor for assigned ISV partners, conducting architectural reviews, POCs, and Well-Architected assessments
- Design, build, and validate scalable cloud-native partner solutions through co-engineering efforts that drive strategic design wins (SDWs)
- Develop reference architectures and best-practice documentation for partner solutions
- Enable partner teams through workshops, immersion days, and hands-on training; support readiness for ISV Accelerate, Competency programs, and Marketplace
- Collaborate with AWS field teams (Account SAs, AMs, Specialist SAs) to drive partner-led customer engagements and pipeline growth
- Track engagement metrics, co-engineering milestones, and strategic design win attainment
- Partner with AWS service teams to advocate for ISV requirements and influence roadmap priorities
- Collaborate across APO on territory strategy, partner prioritization, and joint planning
- Represent AWS at partner events and create technical content (blogs, case studies, whitepapers) showcasing partner success
- Get hands-on building prototypes and demonstrations that communicate the functionality of AWS services.
- Serve as a subject matter expert on manufacturing, enabling field and technical teams to advise customers on adopting partner solutions that run on AWS.

A day in the life
A typical day might include meeting with technical product managers at AWS or with partners, collaborating with others to build and test demonstrations and proofs of concept, and recording or writing technical content such as blog posts and papers. Inclusive Team Culture

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, End User Experience, Amazon WorkSpaces
description:
As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, our vision is to provide business applications leveraging Amazon's unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers' success through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions which solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon's real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager to own End-User Experience across the Agentic WorkSpaces portfolio.

The Agentic WorkSpaces organization envisions a world where people, teams, and AI collaborate securely from anywhere to create unprecedented value for every organization. We build lovable products that empower every business to unlock the full potential of human-AI teamwork, driving smarter decisions, greater creativity, more value, and faster innovation with confidence. This vision is realized through the agentic WorkSpace — a secure, managed environment purpose-built for human-AI collaboration at enterprise scale, where people and AI agents work side by side to deliver results neither could achieve alone.

This is a strategic, portfolio-level role focused on defining how people and AI agents experience, interact with, and derive value from our products. You will establish the end-user experience strategy, principles, and measurable bar across a set of products that span today's human-centered virtual desktop experiences, emerging in-product agentic assistance, and future fully agentic workloads. You will define the experience paradigms for agentic WorkSpaces across the full spectrum of use cases: human workloads, in-app agents that assist people in completing work, and headless or autonomous agentic workloads that operate on behalf of users or businesses. You will ensure that agentic interfaces are cohesive across the portfolio, that product teams are building from a common set of tenets and guidelines, and that the human experience becomes richer and simpler as AI capabilities expand rather than more fragmented or complex.


Key job responsibilities
In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of our end-user personas, their work patterns, and the industry contexts in which they operate. You will clarify how the needs of a call center agent differ from those of an engineer, how a financial advisor's workflow differs from a contractor's, and how autonomous AI agents introduce entirely new experience requirements. You will identify the patterns that cut across personas and industries, distinguish them from requirements that are truly unique, and translate those insights into product direction that individual teams can adopt and execute. You will partner closely with engineering, design, product, go-to-market, and product marketing to shape roadmaps, influence product decisions, and ensure that end-user experience is treated as a strategic differentiator across the organization. You will also own the KPIs that define whether we are delivering a world-class end-user experience. You will establish the right measures of usability, adoption, productivity, agent effectiveness, user trust, task completion, and business value. You will identify where our products fall short, raise the bar across teams, and drive the changes needed to close those gaps.

The ideal candidate is both strategic and deeply customer obsessed. They are curious about how people work, how AI agents will change work, and how enterprise products must evolve as human and agentic workflows converge. They can move comfortably from customer conversations to product principles, from ambiguous future-state thinking to near-term execution, and from portfolio-level strategy to the details that determine whether a product feels intuitive, trustworthy, and indispensable. This is an opportunity to define the end-user experience for a new category of enterprise product: one where humans and AI agents collaborate securely at scale. The person in this role will help shape not just individual features, but the experience model, product bar, and operating principles that guide Agentic WorkSpaces as the portfolio evolves.

We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

title: Consultant - AI Strategy
description:
About MojoTech
MojoTech is an innovative technology consulting firm that leverages strategy, design, data, and software engineering to create results-driven, AI-enabled, digital products and experiences.

We partner with our clients to discover and build tomorrow’s intelligent innovations, empowering every company to unlock future market potential, maximize returns on innovation, and drive transformational change.

About the Role
MojoTech is hiring 2 AI Strategist contractors to support AI product strategy assessments across a private equity portfolio. This is not a prototyping or delivery role. Working across a structured seven-stage methodology (Align, Understand, Scan, Pressure-Test, Validate, Model, Synthesize), you'll form independent judgment on AI features across multiple portfolio companies, spot where AI product opportunities exist, draft every deliverable for senior review, and defend your calls under evaluation from the Director of AI Strategy and the client.

Duration: 9-12 weeks for person 1, 4-5 weeks for person 2

What You'll Do

  • Perform AI strategic assessments per portfolio company and aggregate to cross-portfolio
  • Build feature inventories and workflow maps, analyzing commercial and product analytics data to form an initial view on current-state feature strength
  • Lead the roadmap pressure test per company: draft feature-by-feature critique memos with your own keep/kill/reshape logic, backed by evidence
  • Identify net-new AI opportunity areas within a product, drawing on market and competitor analysis and broader cross-industry AI use-case knowledge, not just reacting to what's already built, on the roadmap or competitor me-too features
  • Compile ranked AI opportunities from customer research and willingness-to-pay (WTP) study inputs, critically evaluating WTP outputs before incorporating them
  • Lead the revised prioritized roadmap and clear action recommendation per company, tying every call to commercial outcome
  • Lead the portfolio-level comparative scorecard, applying the six-dimension rubric consistently across companies and defending scores under challenge
  • Lead relative roadmap strength and priority actions by company at the portfolio level
  • Contribute to feasibility and economics signals to ensure their analysis is accurate and comprehensive
  • Contribute to disruption exposure, normalizing findings against the industry vertical baseline
  • Contribute to investment intensity roll-ups
  • Support the opportunity and risk heat map
  • Use AI-native tools to accelerate your own research, drafting, and synthesis
  • Work concurrently across multiple portfolio companies under tight, overlapping deadlines

What You'll Bring

  • AI degree or equivalent applied background, spanning technical and business-facing AI strategy
  • Experience identifying AI opportunities within a product and connecting them to commercial revenue outcomes (ARR, ACV, retention)
  • Product or project management experience at some point in your career
  • Fluency with AI-native tools to augment your own work
  • Strong structured writing across memos, critique docs, and executive decks
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize and critique conflicting inputs into one defensible recommendation
  • Working knowledge of willingness-to-pay methodology sufficient to critically assess study outputs
  • Comfort applying a scoring rubric consistently and defending it under pushback
  • PE and investment committee fluency: thesis language, hold periods, return thresholds
  • Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple concurrent workstreams

Nice to Have

  • Vertical domain depth across one or more of healthcare IT, life sciences, RegTech/compliance, financial services, or other regulated B2B software markets

Success Looks Like

Your drafts require minimal senior rework. You surface AI opportunities the client hadn't considered. Your critiques and scores hold up under board level scrutiny. Your rubric application is consistent enough to support valid cross company comparison across the portfolio, delivered on schedule despite running multiple companies in parallel. Your portfolio level deliverables, the scorecard, roadmap strength assessment, and priority actions, are accurate and ready for the client without significant rework.

title: GIS Analyst - LiDAR and Remote Sensing
description:
TOTH is seeking a GIS Analyst with experience in LiDAR, point cloud processing, and geospatial data production to join our GIS team. This position will play a key role in processing, analyzing, and validating LiDAR and aerial data used to support engineering, surveying, utility, and infrastructure projects.

This role requires hands-on experience working with LiDAR data and a strong understanding of accuracy, consistency, and quality control. The position will work with complex geospatial datasets to identify potential issues and produce reliable products for use by engineers, surveyors, GIS professionals, and other project teams.

While LiDAR and aerial data processing will be a primary focus, this position will also support broader GIS initiatives, including mapping, data management, utility GIS, automation, and spatial analysis.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

LiDAR, Point Cloud & Remote Sensing

  • Process and analyze UAV and other LiDAR datasets from raw data through final deliverables.
  • Perform point cloud classification, refinement, and quality control.
  • Evaluate LiDAR accuracy using ground control, checkpoints, and established accuracy standards.
  • Identify and troubleshoot alignment, positioning, classification, coordinate system, and other data quality issues.
  • Generate geospatial products including classified LAS/LAZ, terrain and surface models, contours, breaklines, planimetric mapping derived from LiDAR and imagery, orthomosaics, 3D models, profiles, cross-sections, and other project-specific deliverables.
  • Extract features and measurements from LiDAR and imagery for engineering, surveying, utility, and infrastructure applications.
  • Work with aerial imagery, photogrammetry, thermal imagery, and other remotely sensed datasets as project needs require.
  • Apply appropriate coordinate systems, projections, datums, and transformations to geospatial datasets.
  • Perform quality control and validation to ensure deliverables meet project requirements and applicable accuracy standards.
  • Help develop efficient, repeatable workflows and technical standards as our LiDAR and remote sensing capabilities continue to grow.
  • Evaluate new software, technologies, and processing methods that can improve quality, efficiency, or the services we provide.

GIS & Geospatial Support

  • Produce maps, exhibits, spatial analyses, and geospatial datasets supporting engineering, surveying, utility, and infrastructure projects.
  • Support GIS data conversion, migration, schema development, and quality control.
  • Develop and maintain GIS datasets, web maps, feature services, and field data collection solutions.
  • Assist with utility GIS and asset inventory projects involving electric, fiber, and other infrastructure.
  • Automate repetitive GIS and data processing tasks using Python, ArcPy, ModelBuilder, or similar tools.
  • Collaborate with GIS professionals, engineers, surveyors, field personnel, and project managers to solve geospatial problems and develop effective project solutions.

title: Platform Engineer-DevOps
description:
Seqera exists to advance science for everyone through softwareWe provide software for scientists solving today's most complex and important challenges from pioneering innovative therapeutics to unveiling the secrets of our universe. The journey began a decade ago with Nextflow — open software that helps over 100,000 global scientists analyze and process data, with more power and flexibility than ever before.Today, Seqera consolidates fragmented data and diverse computing resources into a unified platform. Our modern biotech stack is trusted by over 150 leading life sciences organizations. Empowered with modern software engineering, organizations conduct science faster, on larger datasets, and with more confidence. Seqera accelerates discoveries in an open world.Would you like to be a part of a company with a bigger purpose and make it successful with your own ideas? If yes, keep reading!

About Seqera

Seqera is on a mission to empower scientists and organizations to solve humanity’s biggest challenges through data-driven science. As the company behind Nextflow and the Seqera Platform, we enable global enterprises, biotech innovators, academic institutions, and public sector organizations to scale complex data workflows with confidence.

We’re a global, remote-friendly team with headquarters in Barcelona and colleagues across the US, UK, and beyond. As we continue to grow, we’re strengthening our internal foundations - and that’s where you come in.

About the role

We are seeking a leader for our Platform Infrastructure team. This role owns infrastructure at Seqera in both directions: the internal platform our engineers build on, and the infrastructure we ship to customers. A large share of our customers experience Seqera through the infrastructure your team produces, which means much of this work is a product surface held to a product's quality bar. You will lead a team of DevOps and security engineers, and you will be a key member in our architecture review process, where infrastructure, security, and operability are weighed at design time alongside every other significant technical decision. This is a leadership role for someone who wants to define how a growing engineering organization builds, ships, and operates. You will report to the CTO.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the reliability, security, and cost-effectiveness of our cloud infrastructure, and the ongoing health of the platform - what gets maintained, upgraded, and retired, not only what gets built.
  • Lead the technical launch of our dedicated single-tenant hosting offering: tenancy and isolation model, provisioning, upgrade and patching strategy across many customer instances, operational tooling, and the per-tenant cost model it will be priced against.
  • Own our Helm charts and Terraform provider as products - versioned, documented, and tested against supported deployment topologies, with the compatibility obligations that customer-deployed infrastructure carries.
  • Own CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and the supported path from empty repo to production, so that teams get pipelines, deployment standards, and observability defaults without assembling them each time.
  • Make cloud cost an engineering discipline: attribution by team and by tenant, anomaly alerting, an efficiency backlog with quantified savings, and cost as an input at design time rather than a surprise after the fact.
  • Lead our security posture in practice - security architecture applied during design review, and the security story we present to enterprise and life-sciences customers.
  • Own our formal incident response: severity definitions, an incident commander rotation, runbooks for our top failure modes, and blameless postmortems that change something.
  • Define what production-ready means at Seqera - tests, observability, documentation, runbooks - and hold the bar consistently across teams.
  • Grow and develop the Platform Infrastructure team, including active hiring at the senior engineer level and active mentorship and career planning for the whole team.
  • Partner with engineering, product, and customer-facing teams to bring infrastructure expertise into decisions early.

About you

You have led infrastructure, platform, or SRE teams with direct accountability for production reliability, and you are still close enough to the work to review it, set the standard, and make architectural calls yourself. You have deep Kubernetes, Helm, and Terraform experience in enterprise settings, and strong opinions about infrastructure-as-code earned from operating it. You have shipped infrastructure that customers deploy and run themselves. You know that charts and modules used by people you will never meet is a different discipline from internal IaC - versioning, backward compatibility, upgrade paths, and support all become your problem. You have real security depth. You can lead a security architecture conversation rather than coordinate one. You treat cloud cost as an engineering responsibility, and you can build cost models that stand up to commercial scrutiny. You have built incident response rather than just carried the pager, and you have handled complex incidents including those involving customer infrastructure. You are comfortable as a technical peer with senior engineers who will challenge you, and equally comfortable presenting to leadership and customers. You write things down. We are moving deliberately from knowledge held by individuals to standards that are explicit, teachable, and enforceable. You are comfortable with ambiguity, and you would rather define a platform than operate one that already exists.

Nice to have

  • Experience with single-tenant, dedicated, or customer-isolated deployment models - fleet provisioning, upgrade orchestration across many instances, isolation guarantees.
  • Developer productivity or internal developer platform experience.
  • Scientific, research, or high-performance computing environments; large-scale batch and data-intensive workloads.
  • Experience with multiple cloud providers.
  • Release engineering experience.
  • Open-source community exposure - much of what we build is used in the open.
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks relevant to enterprise life-sciences customers.

Great benefits

  • Time off: 23 days for vacations per year, 3 days given by Seqera in December, and the national/public holidays according to your location.
  • Equity
  • Private health insurance
  • Private life insurance
  • Home office allowance (valued over 1,000 USD)
  • Subscription to Oliva, Mental Health App
  • Learning and development budget per year (1,000 USD)

title: ACTIVITY LEADER
description:

title: Automation Engineer Apprentice
description:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. The Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) team are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all the robotics and material handling equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!

About the Role:
The Automation Engineering Apprentice(ship) (AEA) will learn to focus on equipment troubleshooting and maintaining material handling equipment (MHE) such as conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, cameras, print and apply labeling systems, scales, HMI systems, and control cabinets. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of this role is to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement.

Amazon AEA apprentices are engaged in the assembly and maintenance of complex machines, plants, and systems in the Reliability & Maintenance Engineering sector or in organizations which purchase and operate such mechatronic systems. Apprentices are paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. They are expected to work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out their work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations.

The successful candidate is an effective communicator, works well in a team, and is self-motivated. They should have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate their activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role.

What Do We Offer?
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there’s more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- You will conduct preventative/corrective maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells
- You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components
- You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc.
- You will assist with basic electronics/Programmable Logic Controllers troubleshooting
- You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
This is a genuinely interesting opportunity for an experienced Senior Data Engineer to join a team that is building out a modern, enterprise-strength data platform and establishing how data engineering is done across the wider organisation.
Snowflake is relatively new within the environment. A strong reference architecture has been established and the focus is now on building upon that foundation, migrating data into the new environment and developing scalable, well-structured data models that can be confidently used across the business.
Importantly, this isn't simply a pipeline-building role.
There is a significant data warehousing and modelling component. You'll work from business requirements through to ingestion, transformation and the creation of robust information layers that enable analysts and other teams to confidently consume and report on data.
You'll also have the seniority and influence to help establish engineering standards, improve ways of working and shape how the platform evolves


What You'll Be Doing
  • Designing and building scalable enterprise data solutions within Snowflake
  • Developing robust dimensional data models and data warehouse structures
  • Building and maintaining complex data ingestion and transformation pipelines
  • Translating business requirements into well-structured, reusable information layers
  • Helping establish data engineering standards, patterns and development practices
  • Working across Snowflake, Azure, SQL, GitHub, Power BI and associated data tooling
  • Supporting the rebuild of legacy data workloads into a modern architecture rather than simply carrying technical debt forward
  • Working closely with analysts, technical teams, stakeholders and external partners
  • Providing technical leadership and mentoring to less experienced team members
  • Contributing to proof-of-concepts, automation and the adoption of new technologies
  • Helping establish sustainable approaches to data quality, governance and platform reliability
  • Longer term, contributing to the evolution of ML and MLOps practices within the data environment
What We're Looking For We're looking for an established Senior Data Engineer rather than someone taking their first step into a senior position.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Significant commercial experience delivering data solutions, ideally 10+ years across data/technology environments
  • Strong hands-on data engineering experience
  • Excellent SQL, ETL/ELT and data warehousing capability
  • Strong experience with schema design and dimensional data modelling
  • Experience designing and building complex, production-grade data pipelines
  • Commercial experience with Snowflake
  • Good understanding of cloud data architecture, ideally within an Azure environment
  • Experience delivering enterprise-scale solutions rather than isolated reporting or analytics projects
  • The ability to understand business problems and translate them into practical data solutions
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to provide technical guidance to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • A willingness to lead, influence engineering practices and help others within the team
Experience with Coalesce, Omnata, Power BI, GitHub or Kimball-style dimensional modelling would be useful, but isn't essential if your core data engineering and modelling experience is strong.

Why Consider This Role?
The attraction here is the opportunity to join at a particularly good stage in the platform's evolution.
The foundations are already in place, so you aren't walking into a blank sheet of paper, but there is still plenty to build, improve and influence. You'll be working with a modern Snowflake architecture, helping determine what "good" looks like as the environment matures.
It's a senior position where you'll remain technically close to the work while having genuine influence over architecture, engineering standards and how data is made available across the organisation.
You'll join a collaborative and relatively young data team, with flexible hybrid working from a central Christchurch office.

If you're an experienced Data Engineer who enjoys the modelling and architecture side of data engineering just as much as building pipelines, we'd be keen to hear from you.

You must have valid New Zealand working rights to be considered for this role

title: Business Intelligence Engineer, Amazon Prime Video Product Analytics
description:
Prime Video is changing the way customers watch movies, TV shows, live events, and channels—offering unparalleled choice and convenience across devices such as Fire TV, mobile phones, game consoles, and connected TVs. We deliver world-class viewing experiences to customers in over 240 countries and territories.

The Prime Video Product Analytics (PVPA) team is a centralized analytics organization supporting the Prime Video Product organization. We bring together Business Intelligence Engineers, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists to deliver comprehensive data tools and insights that drive product decisions and enhance customer experience. Our work spans the full analytics lifecycle—from data infrastructure and pipeline development to advanced analytics, customer insights modeling, AI-driven solutions, and self-service reporting.

This role sits within the PVPA team focused on out-of-app engagement and full-funnel customer journey analytics. Our mission is to understand and optimize how customers discover, engage with, and return to Prime Video—connecting off-app marketing touchpoints (such as email, push, a.com, WhatsApp, search engines, and paid media) with in-app behavior and engagement to build a complete, end-to-end view of the customer experience. We harness data across this full funnel—from acquisition and onboarding through long-term retention—to inform personalization, measure customer engagement and channel effectiveness, and deliver the right content to the right customer at the right time.

Key job responsibilities
We are looking for a highly motivated and experienced Business Intelligence Engineer (BIE) II to join the PVPA team. In this role, you will play a key part in driving customer understanding through data.

You will design and build scalable analytics solutions, self-service reporting tools, and experimentation frameworks, increasingly powered by AI and automation, that give stakeholders across product, marketing, and science a deep, reliable understanding of customer behavior. Your work will directly inform how Prime Video acquires, engages, and retains customers by connecting out-of-app signals to in-app outcomes and enabling faster, more confident decision-making across the organization.

In this role, you will:
* Design and maintain scalable data models, pipelines, and reporting tools that enable accurate and timely marketing performance measurement across multiple customer engagement channels (e.g., email, push, X-site, WhatsApp, paid media).
* Lead the design, execution, and analysis of A/B tests to evaluate marketing strategies, targeting logic, and content variations—ensuring statistical rigor and actionable insights.
* Deliver deep customer insights by analyzing behavioral data and engagement patterns, helping stakeholder and partner teams better understand customer needs, preferences, and responses to messaging.
* Develop dashboards and self-service tools to enable marketers, product managers, and other stakeholders to explore data, monitor performance, and make informed decisions.
* Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams—including Data Scientists, Engineers, Product Managers, and Marketing Managers—to define metrics, surface insights, and influence strategy through data.
* Communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, using data storytelling to highlight opportunities, surface risks, and drive alignment on next steps.
* Champion data accuracy, consistency, and experimentation best practices to raise the overall bar for measurement and insight generation in Prime Video marketing.

title: Sr Product Manager - Tech, Search & Discovery, AbeBooks Onsite Experience
description:
At AbeBooks, we are reimagining how customers discover the millions of printed works available from sellers across the world. As a Senior Product Manager - Technical, you will define the strategic vision for onsite search and discovery, encompassing how customers find, explore, and engage through keyword search, browse and navigation, recommendations, and personalization.

You will own a complex product area, working backward from customer needs to deliver experiences that make discovering rare and unique items intuitive and delightful. You will partner with software engineers, UX designers, and business stakeholders, leveraging advances in semantic search and natural language processing. The problems you solve may not have clear precedents. You will use your expertise and judgment to define the right goals, evaluate emerging technologies, and design long-term solutions.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and own a multi-year product roadmap for search and discovery, balancing short-term customer impact, long-term strategic bets, and technical backlog prioritization.
- Work backward from how customers actually search and browse to identify unmet needs, developing product vision documents (PR/FAQ), and requirements that translate into architecture for search, browse, and personalization systems.
- Establish metrics that distinguish leading indicators from lagging outcomes, using data to identify the highest-leverage improvements across the discovery funnel.
- Evaluate emerging technologies, assessing how to apply them to AbeBooks use cases.
- Lead product development end-to-end, shipping customer-facing experiences across search and discovery while managing cross-team dependencies, driving prioritization consensus, and serving as the bridge between business stakeholders and engineering.
- Build innovative concepts and champion them through senior leadership, on the strategic direction for how customers discover products on AbeBooks.
- Manage bottlenecks, provide escalation management, anticipate and make trade-offs, and balance business needs versus technical constraints to maximize customer value while maintaining system health.
- Mentor and develop other product managers, establishing best practices for experimentation, roadmap planning, and product lifecycle management.

A day in the life
No two days look the same. You might start your morning digging into search performance data, spotting why zero-result queries spiked or whether a new recommendation model is outperforming the baseline. Later, you're in a design review for a browse experience, or sketching how a new discovery feature could help a collector find the obscure edition they're hunting without knowing the exact title. Some days you're writing a PR/FAQ and building the case for investment. Other days you're presenting your roadmap to senior leadership, connecting the dots so the search and discovery experience feels cohesive. When things get stuck, you unblock them.

About the team
AbeBooks offers competitive salaries, a generous benefits package, and personal development days.
What really makes us stand out is the world-class team of people that you get to work with every day. We trust our employees because we only hire the best. We want people who are prepared to challenge the status quo and always raise the bar.

Apply today, and learn more about why you should join our award-winning company.

title: Lab Director & Embryologist
description:
Nevada Center for Reproductive Medicine (NCRM), part of Ivy Fertility, is seeking an experienced Laboratory Director / Senior Embryologist to oversee all laboratory operations while serving as a key scientific and clinical leader within the organization. This position is responsible for the comprehensive management of andrology, embryology, cryobiology, and assisted reproductive technology (ART) laboratory services with a focus on patient safety, clinical outcomes, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.

The Laboratory Director serves as the laboratory's scientific leader and works collaboratively with physicians, clinical staff, and administrative leadership to ensure the highest standards of quality, efficiency, and patient care. This role combines strategic leadership, laboratory oversight, and hands-on embryology expertise.

Essential Responsibilities

Laboratory Leadership & Management

  • Plan, organize, direct, and oversee all embryology, andrology, cryobiology, and fertility laboratory services.
  • Provide overall leadership for laboratory operations, quality initiatives, and strategic growth.
  • Supervise scientific personnel including embryologists, andrology staff, cryobiology personnel, and laboratory technicians.
  • Recruit, train, mentor, evaluate, and develop laboratory staff.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, patient-centered care, and continuous improvement.
  • Partner with physicians and executive leadership to support organizational goals and strategic initiatives.
  • Manage laboratory budgets, equipment purchases, capital expenditures, and operational resources.

Embryology & Clinical Responsibilities

  • Perform and oversee advanced embryology procedures including:
    • Oocyte retrieval processing
    • Conventional insemination and ICSI
    • Embryo culture and assessment
    • Blastocyst development and grading
    • Embryo biopsy
    • Cryopreservation and thawing of oocytes, sperm, and embryos
    • Assisted hatching and other advanced ART procedures
  • Serve as a clinical resource to physicians and patients regarding laboratory procedures and outcomes.
  • Coordinate laboratory-related patient communication and education while helping manage patient expectations.
  • Troubleshoot complex laboratory and embryology issues to ensure optimal clinical outcomes.

Quality Assurance & Regulatory Compliance

  • Maintain responsibility for laboratory quality systems and all activities outlined in the laboratory Quality Assurance Plan.
  • Ensure ongoing regulatory readiness and compliance with:
    • CLIA
    • FDA
    • CDC
    • OSHA
    • ASRM guidelines
    • AAAHC standards
    • Joint Commission standards
    • State and local regulatory requirements
  • Oversee laboratory inspections, accreditation surveys, audits, and corrective action plans.
  • Develop, review, approve, and maintain laboratory policies, procedures, and standard operating protocols.
  • Monitor quality indicators, laboratory outcomes, incident reports, and performance metrics.
  • Lead root cause investigations and implement corrective and preventative actions as needed.

Data Management & Performance Improvement

  • Oversee the accuracy and timely submission of SART data and other required reporting.
  • Utilize laboratory data and metrics to drive quality improvement initiatives and improve patient outcomes.
  • Prepare performance reports and present findings to physicians and leadership.
  • Maintain laboratory databases and evaluate trends impacting clinical success rates and operational performance.
  • Demonstrate competency in data-driven decision making and continuous process improvement.

Equipment & Facility Oversight

  • Ensure the safe operation, maintenance, validation, and optimal performance of all laboratory equipment.
  • Troubleshoot laboratory equipment issues and coordinate service or repairs when necessary.
  • Evaluate and implement new technologies, equipment, and laboratory processes.
  • Maintain laboratory environments that support quality, safety, and regulatory standards.

Strategic & Organizational Leadership

  • Assist in the development and execution of strategic plans to maintain NCRM as a center of excellence in reproductive medicine.
  • Support organizational goals related to patient experience, marketing, growth, and access to care.
  • Develop and maintain strong working relationships with physicians, clinical teams, administrative staff, and referral partners.
  • Manage special projects and other duties as assigned by leadership and the Medical Director.

Qualifications

Required

  • PhD, MD, DO, or other doctoral degree in reproductive biology, medical technology, biological sciences, or a related field.
  • Board certification as a High Complexity Laboratory Director (HCLD) or eligibility to serve as Laboratory Director under applicable regulations.
  • Minimum six years of experience in an ART/IVF laboratory environment.
  • Minimum three years of laboratory leadership or supervisory experience.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of IVF laboratory operations, embryology, andrology, cryobiology, and laboratory quality systems.
  • Extensive knowledge of regulatory and accreditation requirements governing fertility laboratories.
  • Strong leadership, communication, analytical, and organizational skills.

Preferred

  • ABB certification as a High Complexity Laboratory Director (HCLD).
  • Experience serving as a Laboratory Director in a high-volume IVF laboratory.
  • Experience with multi-site laboratory operations.
  • Experience leading accreditation inspections and regulatory audits.
  • Proven success implementing quality improvement initiatives and laboratory growth strategies.

Compensation

Salary ranges from $180,000-$225,000, based on qualifications, board certifications, leadership experience, and laboratory expertise.

About NCRM

Nevada Center for Reproductive Medicine, part of Ivy Fertility, is committed to providing exceptional fertility care through advanced reproductive technologies, outstanding clinical outcomes, and compassionate patient-centered service. Our multidisciplinary team is dedicated to helping individuals and families achieve their goals of building a family while maintaining the highest standards of clinical and laboratory excellence.

title: Health Communications Specialist
description:

Position Summary
The Health Communications Specialist provides communications and analytical support to the Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) at CDC. This role develops, updates, and evaluates health communication materials and strategies related to foodborne, waterborne, environmental, fungal, and parasitic diseases, and supports both routine and emergency public health communications.

Key Responsibilities
Health communication materials and content development
  • Update and create electronic and print materials for public health professionals, healthcare providers, and consumer audiences (fact sheets, newsletters, web pages, social media content, slide decks) using plain language and CDC Clear Communication Index principles.
  • Develop internal communication materials about division accomplishments, news, personnel changes, and workplace policies (internal newsletters, intranet content, organizational charts, leadership emails).
  • Coordinate content development and clearance with internal and external stakeholders and collaborate closely with graphic design staff on layout and presentation.
  • Provide technical assistance on communication and public affairs needs, including sharing CDC resources at educational or stakeholder conferences via exhibits, posters, and presentations.
  • Support division meetings by planning agendas, preparing slides, and providing technical support for web‑based and in‑person meetings.
  • Assist with division web work by reviewing web requests for required materials and clearances, triaging with web developers, and liaising with web staff to implement improvements and resolve technical issues.
  • Review and maintain web content for accuracy, clarity, and alignment with CDC standards, and help users submit web requests as needed.
  • Provide timely follow‑up on inquiries, information requests, and clearance needs, serving as a bridge between subject matter experts and the communications team.
  • Review existing materials for target audiences and collaborate with CDC staff to identify gaps; ensure products are appropriately targeted or tailored for diverse audiences.
  • Identify topics or materials that require formative or summative research, develop research questions with CDC staff, and incorporate findings into communication products.
  • Ensure all communication materials comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements, performing initial 508 remediation on documents and digital content.
  • Develop and disseminate timely, high‑quality scientific and public health information products for the public, target audiences, media, and internal staff, including emergency activations.
