Amazon Operations is the backbone of the Amazon customer experience. With over 50 fulfilment centres, hundreds of delivery stations, and tens of thousands of employees, the team works together to efficiently deliver items to customers. In the fulfilment centres, millions of items are picked and packed annually, while delivery teams work to get orders to customers on time. Safety is the top priority, and the operations culture is defined by teamwork, diversity, and a shared work ethic that keeps the business running smoothly. The team takes pride in delivering the quality service Amazon is known for globally.

As an Amazon operations intern, you'll have the opportunity to apply your analytical skills to impactful projects that enhance the functionality and service of Fulfillment Centers, Sortation Centers, and Delivery Stations. Key aspects of the role include:

Our internships are educational opportunities that allow you, our future managers, to discover how we lead and develop our teams of associates. This internship will place you at the heart of our operations, enabling you to trace the journey of a customer order. You'll gain a realistic job preview of the full-time opportunities awaiting you within our organization.

Opportunities:

title: Consultant - Market Reseacher
description:
About MojoTech
MojoTech is an innovative technology consulting firm that leverages strategy, design, data, and software engineering to create results-driven, AI-enabled, digital products and experiences.

We partner with our clients to discover and build tomorrow’s intelligent innovations, empowering every company to unlock future market potential, maximize returns on innovation, and drive transformational change.


About the Role
MojoTech is hiring a Market Research contractor to build the market and competitive intelligence foundation for AI product strategy assessments across a private equity portfolio. This is not client-facing — you produce the research package that others present and build on. Your work is scoped once per industry vertical and reused across every company assessed in that vertical, so it has to be right, and it has to hold up when a company's roadmap gets measured against it.

Duration: 9 weeks (some weeks full time, some partial)

What You'll Do

  • Lead the market and disruption thesis per 3 industry verticals: pull category AI-trend research using analyst reports and the right tools for PE-grade analysis, scan AI-native entrants disrupting the category, and build the category-level feature-expectation baseline
  • Identify named competitors per company and overlay their position against the industry baseline
  • Contribute competitive evidence, the feature comparison grid and competitor positioning to support roadmap pressure test verdicts
  • Contribute industry vertical category signals and AI-native entrant patterns that seed the ranked AI opportunities list
  • Source the disruption rating that feeds into the portfolio-level disruption exposure roll-up
  • Use AI tools to accelerate research and drafting, while critically evaluating AI-generated output for accuracy and gaps before it goes into any report
  • Write the market and disruption thesis narrative to a depth sufficient for a company's product roadmap to be credibly assessed against it

What You'll Bring

  • Demonstrated experience conducting market and competitive research specifically for private equity clients, with a clear understanding of the depth and rigor PE stakeholders expect
  • Familiarity with the specific tools and sources suited to category-level AI disruption and competitive analysis, not general web search
  • Fluency using AI and deep-research tools to augment research, paired with the judgment to critically evaluate their output for accuracy, hallucination, and gaps
  • A track record of having produced market or disruption thesis reports and competitive feature-comparison baselines before
  • Strong competitive intelligence and product critique writing
  • Executive communication skills, since your output is handed off for others to present and for other roles to build on

Nice to Have

  • Vertical domain literacy in healthcare IT, life sciences, RegTech/compliance, financial services, or other regulated B2B software markets
  • Prior experience specifically on AI strategy assessment engagements

What Success Looks Like

Your industry research is rigorous and reusable enough that every company assessment in that vertical builds on it without rework. Your competitive baselines hold up under board-level scrutiny. Your reports give the AI Strategists enough depth to credibly pressure-test a roadmap against category reality, and your disruption ratings are sound enough to roll up cleanly into the portfolio-level view.

title: SoC Chip Architect, Google Cloud, Silicon
description:
Be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's direct-to-consumer products. You'll contribute to the innovation behind products loved by millions worldwide. Your expertise will shape the next generation of hardware experiences, delivering unparalleled performance, efficiency, and integration.

In this role, you will be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing autonomous solutions that define the next generation of intelligent infrastructure and hardware for the edge. You will contribute to the innovation behind products that transform industries, leveraging your expertise in system-level integration and localized processing to deploy AI models across sophisticated hardware platforms, ensuring intelligence is embedded exactly where the action happens.

As the SoC Architect at Google, you will lead the definition of a groundbreaking first-generation product family. You will bridge the gap between high-level system requirements and detailed chip implementation across domains, collaborating with cross-functional partners to design scalable, energy-efficient, and feature-rich IO SoCs.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving team behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

  • Lead SoC architecture across multiple teams and disciplines, including IP architects, design, verification, validation, firmware, security, power management, software and IP development.
  • Architect and analyze different aspects, including multi chiplets connectivity, chip partitioning, package/board constraints, chip fabric and how SoC subsystems must support them.
  • Define top-level SoC structures, detailing interconnects, clock distribution, and power domains to ensure seamless system integration and operational efficiency.
  • Own the SoC architecture specification and lead it throughout the entire product lifecycle, concept, modeling, implementation, and silicon bring-up.
  • Drive architectural analyses exploring different architectural/implementation alternatives, analyze and recommend the optimal solution balancing between performance, features, power, schedule, and cost.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with functional safety (FuSa) and hardware safety mechanisms designed to meet goals (e.g., ASIL).
  • Experience in defining security architectures, debug infrastructure, and secure boot sequences.

title: Data Center Controls Engineer, Data Center Capacity Delivery - Controls
description:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptable power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

Key job responsibilities
• Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.
• Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. • Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.
• Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.
• Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
• Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.
• Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers. • Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders management.
• Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.
• Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.
• Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
• Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
• Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.
• Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.


About the team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional

title: Front End Associate/Cashier  (82606)
location: 037  College Station  Texas Ave - College Station, TX 77840
description:

3. Greet guests with a smiling face and helpful demeanor, use our Guest Services script based on the division in which they serve. 12. Receive cash, checks, debit cards, credit cards, or gift cards.

18. Call the code for a cash drop as soon as the limit has been reached in order to maintain proper till balance.
19. Keep work area clean and neat and do not overstock counter with merchandise.
20. Count down drawer at end of shift and prepare final drop.
21. Answer questions and provide information to guests.
22. May resolve guest complaints with courtesy and respect.
23. Avoid conversations with coworkers when guests are present.
24. Avoid use of personal cell phone while on the sales floor.
25. Stock shelves and check price tags as needed.
26. Monitor checkout station, making sure all needed tools such as register paper and paper bags are in stock.
27. Prepare assigned areas for inventory and assist in the inventory process if needed.
28. Carry out directives of management efficiently.
29. Fulfill responsibilities with care and attention to detail.
30. Practice teamwork and cooperation with others.
31. Possess time management skills and be able to prioritize tasks.
32. Ability to manage stress in a fast-paced environment.
33. Stand for most of shift, bend and walk occasionally. Use arms, hands, and fingers to feel, handle, reach, and lift. Lift and/or move up to 25 pounds regularly and up to 50 pounds or more occasionally using proper lifting techniques and tools. Push
and/or pull 50-100 pounds or more occasionally. Communicate with and understand team members and guests. See product and payment methods.
34. Work in accordance with all safety regulations of Specs Family Partners and OSHA.
35. Other projects and tasks assigned by management.
Yes, you may have to clean the restroom.
36. Attendance and timeliness are required. It is hard to run the register from home.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty listed above satisfactorily. State law says you must be over the age of 21 to work at Spec's. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. In other words, here's the technical stuff.
Education or Experience
We'd prefer you to have cashiering experience, but if you're willing to learn, we're willing to teach you. We'd like you to have a high school diploma or a general education degree (GED), but sometimes, experience is the best education.
Language Skills
We need you to be able to read, comprehend, and write simple instructions or memos. You must be able to communicate with and understand coworkers and guests. Bilingual skills are a plus.

You need the ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in both whole numbers and in fractions and decimals without taking your shoes off. You need to be able to calculate discounts and percentages. We can provide a calculator.

You need the ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals who need them to perform the essential functions. You must be able to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds regularly and
up to 50 pounds or more occasionally using proper lifting techniques and tools. You must be able to push and/or pull 50-100 pounds or more occasionally. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. This job also requires physical attendance based on a schedule made by management which may vary week to week based on the needs of the business.
Work Environment and Environmental Conditions
We provide a fun and positive environment in which to serve our guests. You may be exposed to outside weather conditions while youre delivering extraordinary service. The noise level is usually moderate.

title: ACES Analyst, ADAT
description:
We are looking for a Business Analyst to join the ACES Data Analytics Team (ADAT) , supporting operational excellence through data-driven dashboarding solutions. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining dashboards and underlying data pipelines that provide actionable insights to operations teams. You will work closely with stakeholders across the support function to translate business needs into analytics solutions that drive decision-making and continuous improvement.

Key job responsibilities
i) Design, build, and maintain dashboards and reporting solutions that support operational performance tracking and decision-making
ii) Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, transform, and analyze data from multiple sources
iii) Develop Python scripts for data manipulation, automation, and advanced analytics
iv) Partner with operations stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into clear technical specifications
v) Perform root cause analysis on operational metrics, identifying trends, anomalies, and opportunities for improvement
vi) Ensure data accuracy and integrity across all reporting and dashboarding deliverables
vii) Proactively communicate progress, blockers, and risks to stakeholders and leadership
viii) Support KTLO (Keep The Lights On) activities for existing dashboards, including troubleshooting, bug fixes, and enhancements

A day in the life
In particular, Business Analysts will support the team with different types of analyses (from estimating the savings of a new project to calculating the drivers behind the Team’s performance) and work with various stakeholders in Amazon’s Operations. We are looking for profiles with analytics and communication skills, business sense and an excellent knowledge of Excel and the Microsoft Office package.
As a Business Analyst on our team, you own the full cycle from raw data to actionable insight. You write SQL queries to pull operational data from multiple sources, validate it, and transform it into something meaningful. When something looks off in the numbers, you investigate — tracing it back through the pipeline until you find the root cause and flag it to stakeholders before it becomes a problem.

You build and maintain dashboards in QuickSuite that operations teams rely on daily. That means designing layouts, connecting calculated fields, setting up filters, and making sure the right people see the right data at the right level of detail. You iterate on these based on feedback, always looking for ways to make the information clearer and more useful.

You also write Python scripts that automate repetitive work — data validations, scheduled extractions, report generation — things that used to take hours manually and now run in minutes. When a quick ad-hoc analysis comes in from a manager, you use Excel to pivot the data and deliver a clean summary without overengineering it.

Throughout all of this, you share what you find. You communicate insights clearly to stakeholders, walk them through what the data is telling us, and help them make decisions based on evidence rather than assumptions.

About the team
Our team sits within the ACES organization and provides analytics and dashboarding solutions that support operational functions. We are a medium size, high-impact team focused on delivering clean, scalable, and well-documented analytics that enable data-driven decision-making across operations. We value seamless development practices, proactive communication, and a strong sense of ownership.

title: Principal Engineer
description:

title: Legal Secretary
description:

title: Director of Accreditation and Licensure
description:
Job Summary

The Director of Accreditation and Licensure provides organization-wide leadership and oversight for accreditation, licensure, and regulatory readiness across RiverValley & Affiliates. The Director serves as the organization’s primary subject matter expert for CARF (Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities) accreditation and oversees applicable national accreditation and state licensure requirements across all programs and facilities in Kentucky, New Mexico, and North Carolina.

The position ensures continuous readiness by monitoring regulatory requirements, coordinating surveys and inspections, maintaining required documentation and renewals, identifying compliance gaps, and overseeing corrective action plans. Working collaboratively with executive, clinical, operational, Quality, Compliance, Legal, and other leaders, the Director integrates accreditation and licensure requirements into everyday operations and quality improvement efforts to support regulatory compliance, service quality, and organizational excellence.

Essential Functions

CARF Accreditation Strategy and Oversight

  • Serve as the organization's primary point of contact and subject matter expert for CARF (Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities) and applicable CARF standards.
  • Maintain a robust CARF readiness plan identifying applicable standards, responsible leaders, required evidence, monitoring activities, and corrective actions.
  • Conduct or coordinate periodic CARF readiness assessments, mock surveys, tracer activities, documentation reviews to identify and close compliance gaps before CARF formal surveys.
  • Prepare and submit all documentation, evidence, and materials required for CARF accreditation surveys.
  • Coordinate the organization's response to CARF surveys, including on-site survey logistics, document preparation, staff scheduling, and support for surveyors during survey activity.
  • Prepare and submit the organization's response to CARF survey findings, including development, submission, and tracking of the Quality Improvement Plan and any required corrective actions following the survey.
  • Monitor changes to CARF standards and survey requirements and translate those changes into clear operational expectations for affected departments, programs, and leaders.
  • Promote continuous CARF readiness throughout the accreditation cycle rather than episodic preparation immediately before surveys.

Additional National Accreditation Compliance

  • Maintain working knowledge of additional national accrediting bodies applicable to the organization's facilities and service lines beyond CARF.
  • Coordinate survey readiness, documentation, and response activities for all additional national accreditations held by the organization.
  • Monitor changes to standards and requirements across all applicable national accrediting bodies and communicate impacts to affected facilities and departments.
  • Maintain a comprehensive organization-wide calendar of accreditation surveys, licensure and certification renewals, regulatory submissions, corrective action deadlines, and other key compliance dates.

National and State Licensure Compliance

  • Maintain expertise regarding applicable facility licensure, program certification, accreditation, and regulatory requirements in Kentucky, New Mexico, North Carolina, and other states in which the organization operates.
  • Ensure timely preparation, submission, and renewal of applicable facility licenses, certifications, and regulatory filings, and coordinate or support certificate of need activities as applicable.
  • Serve as primary liaison to state licensing and survey agencies and applicable national licensing or certification bodies, including coordination of surveys and follow-up visits.
  • Evaluate accreditation, licensure, and certification requirements associated with new programs, service lines, locations, facility changes, acquisitions, and organizational expansion, and advise leadership regarding requirements prior to implementation.

Survey Readiness and Continuous Compliance

  • Develop, review, and revise organizational policies, procedures, and supporting tools to ensure alignment with applicable accreditation, licensure, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with clinical and operational leaders to review department-specific policies and identify required revisions based on changes in accreditation, licensure, or regulatory standards.
  • Maintain a process for identifying changes to accreditation, licensure, and regulatory requirements; evaluating organizational impact; communicating changes to affected leaders; and monitoring implementation.
  • Conduct regular internal audits and rounding to assess ongoing compliance with CARF, other applicable accreditation, and licensure standards.
  • Partner with facility and department leaders to develop corrective action plans and monitor completion of remediation activities.
  • Track and trend survey findings and internal audit results to identify systemic issues and recommend process improvements.

Education and Training

  • Design and deliver training programs for clinical staff, department leaders, and executives on CARF standards, other applicable accreditation standards, licensure requirements, and survey readiness expectations.
  • Develop orientation materials and ongoing education addressing regulatory and accreditation requirements applicable to job function.
  • Serve as an internal resource and educator regarding evolving CARF, other national accreditation, and licensure requirements.

Collaboration with Corporate Compliance and Legal

  • Promptly escalate significant, unresolved, or recurring accreditation and licensure risks to the Vice President of Medical Services and Compliance and other appropriate executive leaders.
  • Support incident investigations, adverse event reviews, and sentinel event analyses from an accreditation and licensure perspective.
  • Assist with responses to regulatory inquiries, complaint investigations, and government audits related to accreditation and licensure.

Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain organized, audit-ready documentation of CARF and other accreditation surveys, licensure filings, findings, and corrective actions for all facilities.
  • Prepare regular reports on accreditation and licensure status, survey outcomes, and readiness metrics for executive leadership and Boards of Directors.

As a Transportation Associate you will:

• Perform various functions within the yard, support site operations teams, internal transportation field teams, and external carriers, as needed, to ensure all trailers arrive and depart on time with zero defects and to maintain workflow for buildings.
• Be professionally trained to operate Commercial Motor Vehicles (CMVs) on non-public roads or in yard to move trailers to/from dock and parking locations.
• Learn Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations and comply with company policies, procedures of those DOT regulations (size, weight, route designations, parking, trailer designations, violation and incident reporting requirements, break periods, etc.)
• Complete driver vehicle inspection reports on equipment and notify managers of any maintenance or delivery issues encountered.

• Opportunity to work outside and drive different commercial motor vehicles in the yard and over the road

Transportation Associates must obtain their Commercial Driver's License (CDL) and Driver Qualification File (DQF) and utilize it as a condition of the role, paid for by Amazon. For Department of Labor/Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration roles (roles for which you receive a CDL), English proficiency is required per federal regulation.

title: Project Engineer, DCCD Construction Ohio
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As a Data Center Project Engineer, you will be part of a creative, diverse team tasked with solving fascinating problems in constructing Amazon Data Centers. Our data centers are industry examples of energy-efficient, cost-effective designs. You will work alongside partner teams such as Operations, Networking, Controls, Security, and Commissioning to build Data Centers that directly support our customers.

As our Data Center Project Engineer, you will support the teams that build some of the most interesting electrical and mechanical systems in the world. You will be on the construction site daily, interacting with construction managers and stakeholders, and be directly responsible for supporting the fast, high-quality delivery of our data center construction. The Data Center Project Engineer will be part of the onsite Construction Management team and will own the communication coordination with our vendors, information workflow, and coordination of document management, including requests for information (RFI), change orders, reports, and schedule updates.

At Amazon, we are all Owners and leverage unique opportunities presented to us by owning everything from the design review to construction bidding to construction execution and final hand-off to our customers. We are a diverse, upbeat, creative team of engineers and managers working on a daily basis to develop innovative data centers for our customers.

Key job responsibilities
The Data Center Project Engineer will be responsible for:

• Leading cross-functional communication and coordination between regional general contractors, stakeholders, and internal teams, ensuring seamless information flow for construction protocols, documentation access, and standardized procedures

• Developing and maintaining comprehensive tracking systems for design modifications, RFIs, and change orders, creating detailed dashboards with priority levels and deadlines for regional leadership review

• Evaluating Method of Procedure (MOP) submissions for thoroughness, necessity, and risk assessment

*Inclusive Team Culture*

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. title: Sr. RF Test Systems Development Engineer, Avionics Verification and Test, Amazon Leo
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

As an Amazon Leo Sr. Satellite RF Test Systems Development Engineer, you will own the full lifecycle of complex RF test systems for spacecraft avionics and payload sub-systems — from architecture and design through production integration and post-delivery support. You will serve as the Responsible Engineer (RE) for your test set, operating at the intersection of hardware design, test automation, and high-rate space flight manufacturing. You should be comfortable with a high degree of ambiguity and relish the idea of solving problems that haven't been solved at scale before. You'll have relentlessly high standards for yourself and everyone you work with, and you'll be constantly looking for ways to improve. We want individuals who want to reach beyond what is possible today. Everyone on the team needs to be entrepreneurial, wear many hats, and work in a highly collaborative environment.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
• Architect, design, build, and sustain RF test systems for satellite payload and avionics units through design validation testing, space qualification testing, production acceptance testing, and on-orbit support
• Own test planning end-to-end: decompose verification requirements into testable specifications, develop test procedures, and lead test readiness reviews
• Drive cross-functional alignment with electrical, mechanical, thermal, software, firmware, and manufacturing teams on verification strategy
• Design and deliver space flight test hardware, fixtures, and tooling that optimize throughput, yield, and fault coverage
• Build quantitative models (test coverage, reliability, throughput) to inform design trade studies and process decisions
• Automate and optimize test processes to meet production rate and first-pass yield targets
• Perform root cause analysis on test failures, lead corrective actions, and drive continuous improvement of production test systems


A day in the life
Our time is balanced between critical support/improvement of an existing factory spaceflight test process and designing future systems. This can be hands-on support troubleshooting test systems or working to align teams around future needs, employing engineering best practices and tools.

The tasks and daily focus change rapidly, and you will often take on exciting new responsibilities to ensure project success. Expect to address complex problems by diving deep into the data, identifying the scope of the issue, and creating innovative and functional solutions.


About the team
This Interdisciplinary Engineer will be a member of the Avionics Verification & Test team working within the wider Satellite RF Hardware Engineering team. This highly collaborative group of engineers has a diverse range of backgrounds and knowledge and works to build scalable and reliable test automation solutions to ensure reliable operation of satellite vehicles in space. The team's responsibilities include design of space payload LRUs: modems, transceivers, LNBs, BUCs and front end modules, process development, test hardware and software development, and test execution supporting our 24/7 high rate satellite manufacturing factory.

Coaching and Field Development

  • Run the coaching system end to end: call coaching, deal coaching, and opportunity inspection alongside sales leadership. You are in live deals every week, not adjacent to them.

  • Own a seller competency model with observable behaviors by stage and by persona. Assess against it, not just train against it.
  • Diagnose precisely. Tell the difference between a skill gap, a knowledge gap, a message gap, and a management gap, then route each to the right fix instead of defaulting to more training.
  • Sit in forecast and pipeline reviews as a contributor: identify the recurring seller behaviors behind slipped and lost deals, and close them.

Category position is the work; the narrative cascade is only the output.

title: Applied Scientist, Alexa Smart Home
description:
Alexa Smart Home Science builds the intelligence that lets customers control and automate their homes naturally, spanning voice understanding, proactive automation, habit and preference learning, and the LLM/agentic systems that power the next generation of ambient home experiences. We are looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to own the scientific direction of a major workstream, turning ambiguous, open-ended problems into production systems that measurably improve the customer experience across millions of homes.
You will define the research agenda for your area, partner deeply with engineering to bring models into production, and raise the scientific bar
across the broader team. You will work at the intersection of large language models, agentic orchestration, personalization, and real-world heterogeneity across homes, devices, and occupants. This is a hands-on role: you will frame the problems, build the models, guide the system design, and mentor other scientists, while influencing product and technical roadmaps beyond your immediate team.

Key job responsibilities
- Independently identify, frame, and solve ill-defined research problems tied to broad Smart Home problem areas, delivering with limited guidance.
- Define system-level technical requirements and partner with engineering teams to adapt scientific techniques to meet production constraints (latency, cost, reliability), making appropriate tradeoffs.
- Own the science strategy and roadmap for a workstream; anticipate future business and technical requirements.
- Design and run rigorous experimentation and evaluation to validate approaches and quantify customer/business impact.
- Build consensus on scientific approach and best practices across multiple teams; influence product features and technical direction beyond your own team.
- Actively mentor and develop other scientists, and raise the bar in hiring.
- Contribute to the internal and external scientific community through publications, patents, and dissemination of scientific artifacts.

A day in the life
No two days look alike, but the throughline is owning a scientific problem from question to production impact. You might dig into evaluation results to find where the experience falls short, frame a hypothesis, and prototype with LLMs or agentic techniques. You will pair with engineering to turn a promising model into a production-ready design, weighing latency, cost, and reliability tradeoffs. Expect alignment with product managers on customer problems, working sessions with fellow scientists, and time mentoring teammates. Your customers are Alexa smart home users across millions of households; your stakeholders span product, engineering, and partner science teams.

About the team
We are the science team behind Alexa's smart home experience. We are applied scientists and science engineers making the home genuinely intelligent: anticipatory, personalized, and effortless. Our mission is to move Alexa from reacting to commands toward understanding a household's rhythms and acting helpfully on the customer's behalf, reliably and at scale. Because no two homes are alike, we embrace that diversity rather than paper over it. We value research-grounded decisions, hands-on work, and long-horizon bets. Scientists own their areas end-to-end, mentor one another, publish, and partner closely with engineering and product.

title: Senior Solutions Architect , Nonprofit Financial Institutions and Credit Unions
description:
Are you the kind of Senior Solutions Architect who thrives when paired to a territory of strategic customers and given the runway to become their most-trusted AWS technical advisor? Do you bring both deep AWS technical breadth and the sensibility to operate inside a mission-driven financial-services organization that treats every technology decision as an extension of its values? AWS is hiring a Senior Solutions Architect to serve as the dedicated SA partner for our Financial Institutions and Credit Unions territory in the AWS U.S. Nonprofits NFICU sub-vertical with $12M+ combined Annualized Revenue across 5 active AWS engagement pillars.

In this role, you will d the broader territory account team (including AWS Professional Services, Customer Solutions, and AWS executive sponsors) to lead the territory AWS technical strategy across an integrated multi-pillar engagement: GenAI Full-Stack, Cloud Migration, Professional Services, and Amazon Connect. You will be the territory customer's primary AWS technical-architect-of-record, the Account Executive's technical co-pilot, and the inside-AWS voice that translates customer's mission, regulatory environment, and operating model into AWS architectural decisions that hold up over the long term.

You will join the AWS WWPS U.S. Nonprofits Solutions Architecture organization — a team that has invested heavily in data-driven SA management, Kiro CLI / agentic-AI tooling for territory and account work, the GenAI Innovation Center (GenAIIC) accelerator mechanism for moving customer PoCs to production, and a strong Sales-SA partnership culture that treats AE quota success and SA technical-advisor outcomes as one shared mission.

The right candidate brings 5+ years of customer-facing technical-advisor or Solutions Architect experience, deep multi-service AWS technical breadth with substantive depth in GenAI on AWS (Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, Amazon Q, Amazon SageMaker), and the judgment and customer-advisor altitude to operate as the technical lead on multi-million-dollar customer relationships. Prior financial services technical experience — fraternal benefit society, life-insurance, wealth-management, or comparable regulated FinServ-adjacent context — is a strong plus, as is direct experience with security-architecture and AI-platform engagements in regulated environments.

If you want to bring your technical depth, customer-advisor instincts, and trusted-advisor patience to a single nonprofit financial-services customer whose mission of helping members live generously aligns with the long-arc patient work that named-account SAs do best, we want to hear from you.



Key job responsibilities
As the Senior Solutions Architect you will:

Own the customer's AWS architectural roadmap end-to-end — discovery → reference architecture → proof-of-concept design → production launch → operational handoff to Customer Solutions Manager (CSM). Author and publish the Workload Solution Document, Architecture Decision Records, and security-and-compliance artifacts that the customer adopts as the canonical AWS-side technical record.

Apply the AWS GenAI Innovation Center (GenAIIC) + AI Development Life-Cycle (AIDLC) accelerator mechanism to move customer GenAI proof-of-concept work into production-launched outcomes.

Partner deeply with AWS Professional Services on customer active ProServe engagements — providing pre-SOW architectural input, mid-engagement technical guidance, and post-engagement production-readiness review.

Translate customer mission, regulatory environment, and operating model into AWS architectural decisions

Operate the Sales-SA partnership cadence with the territory Account Executive — weekly account-team standups, monthly business reviews, quarterly strategic-planning cycles, and ad-hoc executive-engagement support. Mirror the Sales-SA operating model that's already working on the Membership and broader NFICU sub-verticals.

Drive opportunity-pipeline integrity on customer active engagements — keep the multi-pillar opportunity set forecast-honest, keep stale opps moving or honestly retired, and keep the AE bench fed with SA-led architectural advancement actions every week.

Adopt and promote the NPO SA org's Kiro CLI + MCP toolchain for account-management automation — Kiro CLI for customer-engagement preparation, AWSentral / Outlook / TFC-Hub MCP servers for opportunity / activity / TFC tracking. Reduce administrative overhead so technical-advisor hours go to customer outcomes.

Contribute to the AWS NPO Technical Field Community (TFC) — participate in the bi-weekly Kiro demo-build program, the SA-AE mock customer call program, and the GenAI Accelerator Initiative. Where customer engagements yield reusable patterns (e.g., financial-services GenAI architectures), lift those patterns into TFC content that benefits the broader NPO SA bench.

Travel approximately 25-35% for in-person executive briefings, customer workshops, on-site architecture reviews, and joint working sessions, plus AWS / nonprofit industry events such as AWS Imagine for Nonprofits.

A day in the life
A typical week as a territory SA might include a Monday morning standup with the territory Account Executive to review the week's customer-engagement actions; a Tuesday architecture-review session with the customer enterprise architecture team to scope a new agentic-AI use case on Bedrock AgentCore; a Wednesday technical-deep-dive with customer CISO team on the security projects and the AWS Professional Services delivery plans; a Thursday-morning block of Kiro-CLI-automated account-management work that surfaces the multi-pillar opportunity advancement actions; a Thursday-afternoon working session with the AWS Bedrock service team to align customer GenAI roadmap with the latest service capabilities; and a Friday close-of-week cadence with NFICU Sales Manager and SA Manager on customers overall account trajectory and any executive-engagement actions for the next week. Across the month you also block time for in-person trips to customer locations, Workload Solution Document writing on the SCB Financial AI Platform expansion, GenAIIC partner working sessions, and TFC contributions that scale your impact beyond territory accounts into the broader NPO SA org.

About the team
You will join the AWS Worldwide Public Sector U.S. Nonprofits (NPO) Solutions Architecture organization — the team responsible for helping mission-driven nonprofit institutions across the United States use AWS to expand their impact on the communities they serve. Our customers are the country's largest membership associations, federally-aligned nonprofit financial institutions, credit unions, faith-based organizations, healthcare and education foundations, public-broadcasting organizations, environmental and humanitarian nonprofits, and the social-services agencies that operate at the heart of the U.S. social safety net. The technical decisions our customers make — about cloud migration, GenAI adoption, contact-center modernization, data strategy, and security — directly affect the mission outcomes they deliver: members served, donors connected, beneficiaries reached, and lives changed. We treat that responsibility seriously.

You will be a member of the Nonprofits Financial Institutions and Credit Unions (NFICU) sub-vertical SA team within the NPO SA organization. NFICU is the sub-vertical that supports nonprofit financial services foundations, fraternal benefit societies, top U.S. credit unions, and adjacent FinServ-aligned NPO accounts.

How we work is part of what makes this team distinctive. We've invested heavily in data-driven SA management. We've built and adopted the AWS NPO GenAI Accelerator mechanism — a working-group-led initiative that integrates the AWS GenAI Innovation Center (GenAIIC) and AI Development Life-Cycle (AIDLC) frameworks into a repeatable customer-engagement playbook for moving nonprofit GenAI proof-of-concept work into production launches. We run an agentic-AI tooling culture — Kiro CLI, Quick Desktop, and MCP servers (AWSentral, Outlook, TFC Hub) are everyday tools the team uses for territory and named-account management, opportunity progression, customer-engagement automation, and force-multiplied SA hours. We host the AWS Imagine for Nonprofits flagship conference annually and contribute org-wide to its agenda, technical content, and customer round-tables. And we're deeply invested in the AWS Technical Field Community (TFC) — running an SA-AE mock customer call program for SA development, a bi-weekly Kiro demo-build program for SA org-wide capability development, and structured mentoring relationships.

The result is a team where customer obsession isn't a slogan — it's expressed in the way SAs partner with AEs to advance customer outcomes, the way the leadership bench invests in talent growth, the way technical depth and operational rigor are weighted equally, and the way every SA on the bench is given the tools, mentoring infrastructure, and trusted-advisor mandate to do their best work for nonprofit customers whose missions matter. If you want to bring your technical advisor instincts to a single strategic financial-services nonprofit customer whose mission of helping members live generously aligns with the long-arc patient work that named-account SAs do best, this is that team.

title: Steakhouse Room Runner - FT
description:
Position Summary:

The High Steaks Room Runner supports an exceptional Guest experience by ensuring food is delivered from the kitchen to the dining room accurately, promptly, safely, and according to established fine-dining service standards. Working closely with the Servers, culinary team, and restaurant leadership, the Room Runner is responsible for identifying dishes, confirming table and seat positions, delivering each course with proper presentation, and communicating professionally with Guests and team members. Additional responsibilities include assigned side-work, restocking, bussing, and cleaning. Responsibilities must be performed in accordance with all Company standards, policies, and procedures.


Essential Functions:

1. Practice, support, and promote Thunder Valley Casino Resort’s “ELITE” company-wide service mission and demonstrate AAA Four Diamond service standards at all times.

2. Expedite, organize, and garnish orders before delivering to Guests in proper seating order. Deliver food using serving trays and tray jack stands.

3. Verify table numbers, seat positions, menu items, modifications, and special requests before leaving the kitchen.

4. Maintain knowledge of all tables, table numbers, and seat numbers for proper order of delivery of food. Organize orders by table and seat position to support accurate and professional delivery.

5. Properly identify and present each dish when serving Guests.

6. Ensure hot foods are delivered hot and cold foods are delivered cold while maintaining appropriate urgency.

7. Maintain knowledge of the restaurant’s menu, including ingredients, preparation methods, steak cuts and temperatures, sauces, sides, garnishes, and accompaniments.

8. Follow established procedures for serving and clearing from the appropriate side when applicable.

9. Handle plates, trays, serviceware, and other items safely and professionally.

10. Coordinate course timing to ensure all Guests at a table are served appropriately and dishes are delivered at the intended temperature.

11. Communicate with Room Chef and Sous Chefs in the kitchen and the Servers on the dining room floor. Notify the High Steaks front-of-house and back-of house management teams on any production or operational concerns.

12. Maintain food line area with plates, ramekins, serving spoons, soup spoons, demitasse spoons, oyster forks, all sauces, and any applicable garnishes.

13. Restock all items before, during, and after the shift including but not limited to, plates used by the culinary team, service trays, to-go supplies, silverware, flatware, and napkins.

14. Stock all large serving trays and ensure they are clean. Ensure that all tray stands are in their proper location at the bookends of expo line and the end of shift.

15. Maintain bus tubs on the kitchen line including ensuring tubs and labeled appropriately and emptied at the end of the shift.

16. Empty trash and dish bins.

17. Ensure that moist plate wipes available and ensure that expo area is clean and sanitized.

18. Maintain proper sanitizer bucket in station at all times and replace every four (4) hours.

19. Fold napkins as needed by the kitchen for delivered food items.

20. Transport dish trays to the dish pit area. Scrape plates and load glasses and flatware in racks for washing.

21. Ensure that the printer paper, ink, pens, re-fire pad, and note paper are stocked.

22. Perform cleaning duties to maintain the cleanliness and appearance of the restaurant dining area.

23. Maintain professional grooming, appearance, demeanor, and conduct consistent with fine-dining standards.

description:
HealthierHere is a place for people who want to be part of building something that matters. You’ll have opportunities to contribute your ideas, shape our work, collaborate across teams, and help turn ideas into meaningful results in a flexible and supportive environment.

This position will be assigned a hybrid work tier based on the needs of the role, which will determine its in-office expectations. In-office work takes place at our downtown Seattle office.

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

The position requires the ability to participate in meetings, communicate and collaborate with others, and use standard office technology for extended periods. Occasional travel to meetings, events, or partner locations may be required. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, Accessibility, and Belonging

HealthierHere is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive, accessible, and multicultural workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants, prohibiting discrimination or harassment based on race, color, sex, religion, marital status, national origin, age, sexual orientation, citizenship, veteran status, or any sensory, mental, or physical disability, in compliance with local, state, and federal laws. We value diversity, strive for a workforce that reflects the communities we serve, and are committed to building a team where staff from all backgrounds feel they belong, can contribute fully, and are supported to thrive.

Position Overview

The Director of Co-Creation Practice is responsible for building, leading, and scaling HealthierHere Co-Creation & Technical Assistance into a sustainable, revenue-generating service line. The Director provides strategic leadership for practice development, business growth, methodology stewardship, consulting services, and organizational capacity building. This role translates HealthierHere proprietary co-creation methodology into market-ready services that advance community-centered systems change while strengthening the organization's long-term impact and financial sustainability.

This role requires a practitioner with deep expertise in co-creation and community-centered design, and the organizational development skills to develop an infrastructure of a consulting practice from the ground up, establish market positioning, operationalize the service line, and the judgment to hold the integrity of the methodology while navigating client priorities, competing timelines, and institutional power dynamics.

Key Responsibilities

Practice Leadership & Business Development

  • Drive publication and dissemination efforts establishing HH as a methodology leader in the field.
  • Build, launch, and lead HH’s Co-Creation Consulting & Technical Assistance service line, developing the organizational infrastructure, service offerings, pricing structure, and client engagement model from the ground up.
  • Develop and execute a business development strategy: identify target clients, build a consulting pipeline, and secure external contracts across government, health systems, academic, and nonprofit sectors.
  • Manage client relationships across the full engagement lifecycle, from proposal and scoping through delivery, evaluation, and close.
  • Track real cost, time, and capacity data from live engagements to produce evidence-based financial projections and inform the service line business plan and sustainability model.
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to integrate co-creation into HH’s existing business lines, including Connect2 Technology, Super Hub, and statewide CIE.
  • Design and implement the strategic vision, annual operating plan, and growth strategy for the Co-Creation Practice, ensuring alignment with HealthierHere organizational priorities.
  • Develop, manage, and monitor the practice's annual operating budget, ensuring sound financial stewardship, resource allocation, and long-term sustainability.
  • Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for the practice, using data to evaluate client outcomes, financial performance, operational effectiveness, and organizational impact.
  • Monitor industry trends, client needs, and emerging opportunities to inform practice growth, service innovation, and competitive positioning.

Staff Leadership & Team Development

  • Recruit, develop, coach, and evaluate consulting practice staff, fostering a high performing, collaborative team while supporting distinguishing roles in training delivery, co-creation facilitation, and business development as the practice scales.
  • Design organizational capacity by integrating co-creation models, principles, tools, and practices across HH’s programs, operations, and cross-function initiatives.
  • Develop and maintain the Internal Co-Creation Playbook, which serves as the practitioner’s guide integrating the methodology, tools, SOPs, and facilitation scenarios drawn from live engagement experience,
  • Establish role-clarity frameworks that distinguish consulting functions from internal program staff functions as the practice grows.
  • Serve as a strategic leader within HealthierHere by contributing to cross-functional planning, organizational initiatives, and enterprise decision-making.

Certificate Training Program

  • Oversee the design, development, delivery, and iteration of HH’s co-creation certificate training program.
  • Develop training curriculum, facilitation guides, simulation exercises, and certification standards in collaboration with practice staff.
  • Establish and manage the pipeline of certified co-creation practitioners, with attention to volume, pricing, and long-term sustainability.
  • Identify which curriculum elements are ready for external delivery and which require further field-testing or development, iterating the program after each cohort.

Practice Dissemination & Thought Leadership

  • Lead publication efforts on HH’s co-creation methodology, producing white papers, peer-reviewed articles, and practitioner-facing resources that establish HH as a methodology leader in the field.
  • Represent HH at conferences, convenings, and peer networks presenting the methodology, building visibility, and generating referral relationships that feed the consulting pipeline.
  • Operationalize and sustain partnerships with peer organizations, academic institutions, and field leaders to advance both the methodology and HH’s market position.
  • Regularly contribute to the field’s understanding of what systems co-creation intermediaries do and why it matters for health equity.

title: Space Systems Modeling and Analysis Engineer
description:
We are seeking a Space Systems Modeling and Analysis Engineer to develop and deploy high-fidelity computational models of multi-orbit space architectures supporting satellite communications (SATCOM), navigation warfare (NAVWAR), space-based sensing and targeting (SBST), and missile warning and tracking (MWT) missions. In this role, you will build fast, parallelizable simulations of proliferated constellations across LEO, MEO, and GEO. You will model space-to-space crosslinks, space-based RF and EO/IR sensors, as well as ground segment architectures. You will perform constellation-level operational availability analysis that goes beyond link coverage to account for real-world operational impacts such as downtime due to routine on-orbit maintenance, ground gateway availability, and disturbances from both ground- and space-based threats. You will support trade studies on constellation design, link budgets, timing architectures for alternative positioning/navigation/timing (Alt-PNT) frameworks, and sensor coverage geometries. Your work will directly inform architecture decisions that ensure resilient space systems in contested and degraded environments.

Key job responsibilities
- Develop, validate, and maintain high-fidelity models of multi-orbit constellations (pLEO, MEO, GEO) for SATCOM, NAVWAR, SBST, and MWT mission areas
- Design and execute large-scale, parallelizable simulations to evaluate constellation performance, coverage, and resilience under nominal and degraded conditions
- Perform trade studies and sensitivity analyses on constellation design parameters, sensor geometries, and network topologies
- Model ground segment architectures including radar systems, ground entry points, and ground-based command and control infrastructure
- Model space-based threats including maneuverable satellites, counter-space systems, and electromagnetic warfare effects on space architectures
- Model Alt-PNT frameworks including timing budget analysis and navigation warfare scenarios
- Analyze Space Data Network (SDN) architectures including space-to-space crosslinks, exchange points, and network service orchestration
- Develop sensor performance models for multi-phenomenology detection (infrared, radar) across missile warning and moving target indication missions
- Support architecture decisions by quantifying system resilience, capacity, and performance under adversarial conditions
- Produce technical documentation, trade study reports, and briefings for engineering and program leadership
- Collaborate with systems engineers, mission architects, and government stakeholders to translate operational requirements into simulation parameters

Export Control : This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a US Government security clearance of TS/SCI.

title: Aerospace Hardware Development Engineer, LEO
description:
At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you.

Amazon Leo is looking for an Aerospace Hardware Development Engineers to design and optimize circuitry for satellite systems and develop proof of concept prototypes for next-generation satellite hardware. This role requires close collaboration with radiation, power, mechanical, thermal, RF, and software teams. Responsibilities also include designing automated test systems, test fixtures, and factory tests, as well as leading bring-up and qualification test campaigns.

This is a fast-paced, intellectually challenging opportunity to work with thought leaders in multiple technology areas. You'll have relentlessly high standards for yourself and everyone you work with, and you'll be constantly looking for ways to improve. We want individuals who want to reach beyond what is possible today. Everyone on the team needs to be entrepreneurial, wear many hats and work in a highly collaborative environment. Our team is responsible for delivering flight-qualified hardware that enables thousands of satellites to fly.

As an Amazon Leo Aerospace Hardware Engineer you will work with multiple engineering teams across ground and space systems to design, analyze, build, and test hardware assemblies and components for satellite applications. Your focus will be on hardware development from concept through qualification, supporting the introduction of new generations of satellites.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and validate hardware components, assemblies, and software solutions—from circuit boards and integrated subsystems to onboard power management systems—to determine suitability for flight.
- Develop closed-loop control algorithms leveraging sensor peripherals, microcontrollers, and custom silicon, as well as innovative hardware designs and processes to optimize spacecraft capabilities.
- Implement hardware design strategies to mitigate product risks to stakeholders.
- Work with avionics, payload, radiation, power, mechanical, thermal, RF, and software teams to gather requirements, develop hardware architectures, determine applicable design constraints, and prepare for hardware integration.
- Collaborate with responsible engineers, manufacturing engineers, software developers, tooling teams, and ground support teams to deliver flight-qualified hardware ready for launch and ensure every Leo device shipped meets requirements.
- Communicate fluidly across teams to identify hardware design risks and how they will be addressed to ensure mission success.
- Enable data-driven performance insights through automated test execution, collection, and analysis pipelines, including complex test automation sequences using scripting languages such as Python.
- Work hands-on with hardware test equipment.
- Define and execute software release processes, CI/CD, and quality verification.
- Deliver clear documentation and user-focused software for engineering and manufacturing teams.

About the team
Amazon LEO is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon LEO will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.

title: Business Intelligence Developer
description:
Company Overview

Index Analytics, LLC, is a rapidly growing, Baltimore-based small business providing health-related consulting services to the federal government. At the center of our company culture is a commitment to instilling a dynamic and employee-friendly place to work. We place a priority on promoting a supportive and collegial team environment and enhancing staff experience through career development and educational opportunities.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Junior BI Developer with foundational SQL, reporting, and data analysis skills, strong attention to detail, and a desire to build expertise in business intelligence development. This role is ideal for an early-career professional interested in developing hands-on experience with SAP BusinessObjects, enterprise reporting solutions, and business intelligence technologies in a federal client environment.

Working under the guidance of senior developers, analysts, data teams, and business stakeholders, the Junior BI Developer will support the development, maintenance, testing, and troubleshooting of enterprise reporting solutions using SAP BusinessObjects, SQL, and related analytics tools. Responsibilities include assisting with report and universe development, creating and validating SQL queries, testing and validating report outputs, documenting report logic and technical specifications, and supporting ongoing reporting operations and production issue resolution.

This position provides exposure to the full reporting solution lifecycle, including requirements analysis, design support, development, testing, deployment, maintenance, and continuous improvement of analytical products and reporting applications within enterprise business intelligence environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain machine learning and deep learning models, including both traditional (e.g., regression, tree-based models) and neural network-based approaches.
  • Build and deploy end-to-end ML pipelines on AWS (e.g., SageMaker, S3, Glue) for scalable training, evaluation, and inference.
  • Develop and implement advanced NLP solutions, including text classification, entity recognition, topic modeling, and semantic search using models such as BERT and transformer-based architectures.
  • Design, build, and productionize RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems, including document ingestion, embedding pipelines, vector search, and LLM orchestration.
  • Design and implement a scalable knowledge graph and semantic data model that captures relationships among policies, analytic use cases, data domains, information assets, products, and institutional knowledge, enabling advanced search, discovery, impact analysis, and AI-assisted knowledge retrieval.
  • Develop LLM-powered applications, including prompt engineering, evaluation frameworks, and optimization techniques for accuracy, consistency, and cost.
  • Contribute to agentic AI system design, including multi-step reasoning workflows, tool use, and orchestration of LLM-driven agents for complex tasks.
  • Implement predictive analytics and statistical modeling to uncover patterns, trends, and insights from healthcare data.
  • Perform data mining and exploratory data analysis (EDA) using state-of-the-art techniques across structured and unstructured datasets.
  • Build data visualizations, dashboards, and analytical tools to communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics (e.g., accuracy, AUC, precision/recall) and present results in a clear, actionable manner.
  • Collaborate in an Agile environment with cross-functional teams including engineers, analysts, and stakeholders.
  • Recommend data-driven solutions and AI strategies aligned with CMS business needs and healthcare policy objectives.

  • Architect and optimize Siemens team center solutions, managing the configuration, installation, maintenance, and ongoing support of teamcenter PLM application, including integrations with CAD applications.

title: Systems Development Engineer II, Amazon Robotics Infrastructure Engineering

From two million square foot automated robotics fulfillment centers to small last-mile delivery stations in emerging markets, these networks are the backbone of Amazon Operations. You will tackle complex, novel situations every day and have the opportunity to work with multiple technical teams at Amazon in different locations. title: Senior Cloud Hardware Development Engineer, AWS Hardware Engineering Services, Specialized Platforms and Servers
description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering Services (HWEngS) owns the new product development (NPI) and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain, and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers, and you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Cloud Hardware Development Engineer (CHDE): The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering Services (HWEngS) Specialized Platforms and Server team creates Enterprise rack solutions for Amazon’s innovative web services. We are seeking experienced CHDEs to architect, design, develop, and build next-generation server and rack solutions. Our designs are industry-leading in performance, frugality and operational excellence, and are critical to the success of the AWS business and the more than one million customers who use AWS today. Our CHDE's solve challenging technology problems, and build architecturally sound, high-quality servers and rack solutions to enable AWS to realize critical business strategies

Key job responsibilities
As a Senior CHDE you will be responsible for bringing new technology to our server & products as well as scaling how we operate our massive existing & rapidly growing fleet.
You will collaborate with internal development teams and external suppliers to deliver new servers with industry leading performance and quality.
You will establish strategic vision and drive execution in defining and delivering new products and services.
You will lead the integration and delivery of servers, support the development of automated monitoring, and failure analysis services to operate, debug, and scale our servers.
You will work closely with other AWS software teams to tailor and operate servers solutions for the AWS environment.
You will support launching our servers into production and operating our fleet of servers.

What you will do:
As a member of the Specialized Platforms and Servers team, you’ll be responsible for integration of hardware/software components to build our servers, working with service teams to define products. You will interact with engineers across the company and work with an interdisciplinary team to execute product designs from concept to production including design, development, validation, and the deployment of servers at scale.

You will solve design challenges across many disciplines including server/board design, thermal-mechanical design, server firmware/software, integration into our software service control plane, manufacturing, and data center operations.

You will deliver functional block diagram, schematics, specifications, analysis, test plans, and monitoring plans used to build our servers and components. You will work closely with internal teams, suppliers, and external partners to ensure our designs are of the highest quality.

The team is comprised of CHDE's, System Development Engineers and Technical Program Managers, all with the common goal of delivering the best specialized server fleet possible to our customers.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
